Verdict

Reviewed 28 Oct 2026 · next 26 Jan 2027

Not needed. MIT and public, but a 1-star fork of dagrejs/dagre pinned at 3.1.1 while upstream is 3.1.3, and it is not used by the NVL layout-workers package. Use @dagrejs/dagre directly.

Current Reviewed version 3.1.1 Requirement: Graph visualization in a React application

Reasoning

  1. MIT licence and a public repository (neo-technology/dagre), so the hard licence constraint does not apply.
  2. It is a fork of dagrejs/dagre; upstream is at 3.1.3 (Oct 2026) while the fork ships 3.1.1.
  3. @neo4j-nvl/layout-workers depends on @dagrejs/dagre 3.1.1, so adding this fork creates a second dagre copy with no functional gain.
  4. Only 3 published versions and no provenance.
  5. No OSV advisories.

Caveats

  • If Neo4j-specific patches are required, document them first; nothing in the package metadata says what they are.

Decision context

Approved

cytoscape is the primary choice for Graph visualization in a React application. This package is classified as Rejected.

The NVL suite is denied: its LICENSE.txt limits use to Neo4j Aura or commercial Neo4j, it publishes no repository, carries no provenance and cannot be loaded by Node in either module system. 1.2.2 was checked separately: same licence and packaging, different layout stack, so the denial applies to both. Adopt Cytoscape.js as the primary renderer: MIT, zero dependencies, SLSA provenance, active, 138 KB gzip, and layouts via extensions. Use the core API with a ref or a thin internal wrapper because react-cytoscapejs is stale. Adopt Sigma.js as the fallback for large graphs: MIT, WebGL, 110 KB gzip and active, but client-only (WebGL2) and without provenance; pair it with graphology and @react-sigma/core. Hold @antv/g6 (88 MB, 104 packages, 413 KB gzip, 333 open issues, no release in 90 days) and @xyflow/react (excellent node editor, but not an exploration or layout engine).
